rows.note: This is the all-purpose everyday term for money earned from work, covering both wages and salary.

example.english: When will I get my pay?
example.jyutping: ngo5 fan6 jan4 gung1 gei2 si4 ceot1

rows.note: Use this colloquial term when referring to someone’s regular pay, especially wages or a monthly salary.

example.english: Has this month's pay been paid yet?
example.jyutping: gam1 go3 jyut6 ge3 loeng4 ceot1 zo2 mei6 aa3

rows.note: Use this formal term for salary or remuneration, especially in official or written contexts.

example.english: Please refer to the contract for details of the pay arrangements.
example.traditional: 有關薪金安排，請參閱合約。
example.jyutping: jau5 gwaan1 san1 gam1 on1 paai4 cing2 caam1 jyut6 hap6 joek3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice for handing over money, settling an obligation, or paying for a cost.

example.english: We pay after we finish eating.
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 sik6 jyun4 faan6 sin1 bei2 cin2

rows.note: Use this for the attention slice of “pay attention”; tribute and visits use different Cantonese verbs.

example.english: We need to pay attention to changes in the weather.
example.jyutping: nei1 paai4 jiu3 lau4 ji3 tin1 hei3 bin3 faa3

rows.note: Use this when an action or investment is worthwhile, advantageous, or yields a benefit rather than when money is literally paid.

example.english: You pay less and get a better deal by buying two.
example.traditional: 買兩件抵好多，咁樣做有着數。
example.jyutping: maai5 loeng5 gin6 dai2 hou2 do1 gam3 joeng6 zou6 jau5 zoek6 sou3

rows.note: Use this for suffering a consequence or paying a price for something one has done.

example.english: If you do something wrong, you have to pay the price.
example.jyutping: zou6 co3 si6 zau6 jiu3 fu6 ceot1 doi6 gaa3
